2) Implementation for @supports syntax and format (REQ-SUPPORTS-PARSE, REQ-FORMAT-VALIDATION, REQ-MIXED-SUPPORT): - src/rules/valid-annotation-format.ts: - Imports helpers from ./helpers/valid-implements-utils and defines validateImplementsAnnotation(), which delegates to validateImplementsAnnotationHelper with MIN_IMPLEMENTS_TOKENS and reporting helpers. - processCommentLine() detects @supports via `const isImplements = /@supports\b/.test(normalized);` and, when present, strips the tag and calls validateImplementsAnnotation immediately, without affecting the pending multi-line state for @story/@req: - Comment: "// Handle @supports as an immediate, single-line annotation" and JSDoc requirement tags: `@req REQ-IMPLEMENTS-PARSE`, `@req REQ-FORMAT-VALIDATION`, `@req REQ-MIXED-SUPPORT` under docs/stories/010.2-DEV-MULTI-STORY-SUPPORT.story.md. - meta.messages.invalidImplementsFormat is documented for this story and produces "Invalid annotation format: {{details}}.", with details built by valid-implements-utils (e.g., mentioning @supports and expected story/req examples). - The rule description explicitly includes @supports: `description: "Validate format and syntax of @story, @req, and @supports annotations"`. - src/rules/helpers/valid-implements-utils.ts: - Documented as helpers for @supports validation for this story with @req REQ-SUPPORTS-PARSE, REQ-FORMAT-VALIDATION, REQ-MIXED-SUPPORT. - MIN_IMPLEMENTS_TOKENS = 2 enforces minimum of story path + one requirement ID. - parseImplementsTokens(): - Trims the raw value (text after @supports), splits on whitespace, and enforces MIN_IMPLEMENTS_TOKENS. - Returns `{ storyPath, reqIds }` where storyPath is first token, reqIds is rest — exactly `@supports story-path REQ-ID1 REQ-ID2 ...`. - On missing value or insufficient tokens, calls reportMissingImplementsValue or reportMissingImplementsReqIds, which emit invalidImplementsFormat diagnostics with explicit @supports examples. - validateImplementsTokens(): - Validates storyPath with options.storyPattern; on failure, calls reportInvalidImplementsStoryPath with a message pinpointing the story path and expected example. - Iterates reqIds and, for each invalid ID (not matching options.reqPattern), calls reportInvalidImplementsReqId which reuses the existing invalidReqFormat message via buildReqErrorMessage. - validateImplementsAnnotationHelper() wires both together: parse tokens, then validate them, satisfying REQ-SUPPORTS-PARSE and REQ-FORMAT-VALIDATION.
3) Deep requirement validation for @supports (REQ-SUPPORTS-VALIDATE, REQ-ERROR-CONTEXT, REQ-SCOPED-IDS, REQ-MIXED-SUPPORT): - src/rules/valid-req-reference.ts: - Defines IMPLEMENTS_TOKENS = { STORY_INDEX: 1, FIRST_REQ_INDEX: 2 } for @supports token layout with a JSDoc for docs/stories/010.2-DEV-MULTI-STORY-SUPPORT.story.md. - parseImplementsLine(line): - Splits the full line, extracts `storyPath = parts[1]` and `reqIds = parts.slice(2)`, returns null if missing storyPath or req IDs; this matches the `@supports story-path REQ-ID...` contract (REQ-IMPLEMENTS-VALIDATE, REQ-SUPPORTS-PARSE equivalent at deep layer). - validateImplementsLine(): - Calls resolveStoryAndRequirements() with storyPath, which uses validateAndResolveStoryPath to reject path traversal and absolutes (reporting `invalidPath`), and loadAndCacheRequirements() to build a Set of requirement IDs found in that specific story file. - Iterates all reqIds and calls checkRequirementExists() for each; if absent in the Set, reports `reqMissing` with data { reqId, storyPath }. - Since reqCache is keyed by resolvedStoryPath and requirement IDs are looked up per story file, requirement IDs are scoped per story (REQ-SCOPED-IDS). The passing test "multi-story supports with shared requirement IDs" demonstrates that the same REQ-SHARED-ID can appear in multiple story files without conflict. - handleAnnotationLine() dispatches between line types: - `@story` lines update storyPath. - `@req` lines are validated against the current storyPath. - `@supports` lines call validateImplementsLine() directly, keeping @supports and @story/@req mixed usage supported in a single comment (REQ-MIXED-SUPPORT). - meta.messages.reqMissing is defined as: "Requirement '{{reqId}}' not found in '{{storyPath}}'" and tests assert both reqId and storyPath in data, satisfying REQ-ERROR-CONTEXT.
4) Treating @supports as satisfying story and requirement presence (REQ-REQUIRE-ACCEPTS-SUPPORTS, REQ-BACKWARD-COMPAT, REQ-MIXED-SUPPORT): - src/rules/helpers/require-story-io.ts (used by require-story-annotation): - commentContainsStory() returns true if a comment's value contains "@story" OR "@supports"; JSDoc explicitly references docs/stories/010.2-DEV-MULTI-STORY-SUPPORT.story.md and REQ-REQUIRE-ACCEPTS-IMPLEMENTS. - scanLinesForMarker() and fallbackTextBeforeHasStory() also treat any line/text containing "@story" OR "@supports" as evidence the function is already annotated, with comments tying this to REQ-REQUIRE-ACCEPTS-IMPLEMENTS. - hasStoryAnnotation() (in src/rules/helpers/require-story-helpers.ts) composes jsdocHasStory, commentsBeforeHasStory, leadingCommentsHasStory, linesBeforeHasStory, parentChainHasStory, and fallbackTextBeforeHasStory. Because those use commentContainsStory, @supports counts as a story marker. - Rule tests (tests/rules/require-story-annotation.test.ts) include the case `name: "[REQ-REQUIRE-ACCEPTS-IMPLEMENTS] valid with only @implements annotation"` whose code uses `@supports ...`, ensuring a function with only a @supports line is considered valid and does not trigger missingStory. - src/utils/reqAnnotationDetection.ts (used by require-req-annotation via checkReqAnnotation): - commentContainsReq() returns true when comment.value includes "@req" OR "@supports". - linesBeforeHasReq(), parentChainHasReq(), and fallbackTextBeforeHasReq() all treat both @req and @supports as requirement markers when scanning surrounding lines, parent comments, and fallback text windows. All are tagged with REQ-REQUIRE-ACCEPTS-IMPLEMENTS and docs/stories/010.2-DEV-MULTI-STORY-SUPPORT.story.md. - hasReqAnnotation() combines: - advanced heuristics (linesBeforeHasReq, parentChainHasReq, fallbackTextBeforeHasReq) that look for "@req" OR "@supports" around the node. - direct checks: jsdoc.value/includes("@req" or "@supports") and comments.some(commentContainsReq). - Because require-req-annotation's create() simply calls checkReqAnnotation() for nodes it wants to inspect, any nearby @supports line counts as satisfying the requirement-annotation requirement. - tests/rules/require-req-annotation.test.ts verifies this with the valid case `"[REQ-REQUIRE-ACCEPTS-IMPLEMENTS] valid with only @implements annotation"` using a @supports line only; the rule reports no missingReq error, confirming REQ-REQUIRE-ACCEPTS-SUPPORTS while keeping old @req semantics intact (REQ-BACKWARD-COMPAT). - Numerous existing tests in the same file still assert that plain, unannotated functions are invalid and that @story-only annotations are insufficient, proving backwards compatibility of previous behavior.
5) Backward compatibility and mixed usage (acceptance criteria: Backward Compatibility, Mixed Usage): - All legacy behaviors for @story and @req remain tested and passing: - tests/rules/require-story-annotation.test.ts and tests/rules/require-req-annotation.test.ts have many valid/invalid cases using only @story and only @req, covering function declarations, expressions, methods, TS declarations, and scopes/exportPriority. - tests/rules/valid-annotation-format.test.ts has extensive coverage for @story/@req formatting (single-line, multiline, configurable patterns, invalid config) which all passed in the Jest run. - tests/rules/valid-req-reference.test.ts covers @story+@req deep validation (missing requirements, path traversal, abs paths) in addition to the @supports cases. - Mixed usage explicitly tested: - In valid-annotation-format.test.ts: `"[REQ-MIXED-SUPPORT] valid mixed @story/@req/@supports usage in same block comment"` shows a block with all three annotation types that must pass the rule. - In deep validation, handleAnnotationLine() accepts both @story/@req and @supports lines for the same comment; tests for multi-story supports confirm they do not interfere with standard @story/@req behavior.
6) Error messages including story context (acceptance criterion: Error Messages, requirement REQ-ERROR-CONTEXT): - src/rules/valid-req-reference.ts meta.messages: - reqMissing: "Requirement '{{reqId}}' not found in '{{storyPath}}'" — includes both the missing requirement ID and the story path. - invalidPath: "Invalid story path '{{storyPath}}'". - tests/rules/valid-req-reference.test.ts asserts the `storyPath` field in data for both @story and @supports cases, e.g.: - Missing requirement for @story: data { reqId: "REQ-NON-EXISTENT", storyPath: "docs/stories/001.0-DEV-PLUGIN-SETUP.story.md" }. - Missing requirement for @supports: data { reqId: "REQ-NOT-IN-A", storyPath: "tests/fixtures/story_multi_a.md" }. - src/rules/helpers/valid-implements-utils.ts constructs invalidImplementsFormat messages that embed the offending story path and the expected example, e.g.: - `Invalid story path "invalid/path.txt" for @supports annotation. Expected a path like "docs/stories/005.0-DEV-EXAMPLE.story.md".`
7) Documentation and migration guidance (acceptance criterion: Documentation): - docs/rules/valid-annotation-format.md: - Declares this rule as supporting `@story`, `@req`, and `@supports` and references docs/stories/010.2-DEV-MULTI-STORY-SUPPORT.story.md in its header. - Has a dedicated section "Migration to `@supports`" with: - When to keep @story + @req vs when to adopt @supports. - Before/After examples of multi-story integration functions using both styles. - Mixed usage guidance explaining incremental adoption of @supports, explicitly mentioning that both styles are supported simultaneously. - user-docs/migration-guide.md: - Section 3.1 "Multi-story `@supports` annotations" gives a concrete example of @supports usage. - Later sections show a before/after example where applyFilters() uses both @story/@req and @supports lines, explaining how valid-annotation-format and valid-req-reference jointly validate @supports annotations. - The guide emphasizes that existing @story + @req annotations remain valid and that @supports is primarily for multi-story integration, aligning with REQ-BACKWARD-COMP and REQ-MIXED-SUPPORT. - README.md and user-docs mention the `traceability/prefer-implements-annotation` rule as a migration tool towards @supports; the README line explicitly says it recommends migration to `@supports`.
8) Conformance with ADR 011 (rename @implements → @supports): - Runtime behavior uses `@supports` exclusively for user annotations: - All parsing and detection logic for multi-story annotations in valid-annotation-format.ts, valid-implements-utils.ts, valid-req-reference.ts, require-story-io.ts, and reqAnnotationDetection.ts look for the string "@supports"; none of the runtime code checks for a user-level "@implements" tag. - Remaining `@implements` mentions found via grep are in traceability comments (e.g., `// @implements docs/stories/...`) and developer documentation, not in user-facing parsing logic. - docs/decisions/011-rename-implements-to-supports-annotation.accepted.md states that @implements is no longer recognized by the plugin and must be updated to @supports; the current implementation aligns with that: only @supports is parsed and validated in user code.
9) Test suite status: - `npm test -- --verbose` runs Jest with all 36 test suites passing (277 tests, 0 failures). This includes all rule tests that specifically reference docs/stories/010.2-DEV-MULTI-STORY-SUPPORT.story.md and the REQ-* IDs defined in this story, providing concrete execution evidence that the implemented behavior matches the specification.
traceability.notes: The 010.2-DEV-MULTI-STORY-SUPPORT story is fully implemented. The plugin supports the @supports story-path REQ-ID... format, validates its syntax and semantics (including per-story requirement existence), and treats @supports as satisfying both story and requirement presence checks in require-story-annotation and require-req-annotation without breaking existing @story/@req behavior. Mixed usage of @story/@req/@supports within the same comment is supported and covered by tests. Error messages from valid-req-reference include the checked story path, and requirement IDs are scoped per story file via a per-path requirement cache. Documentation in docs/rules/valid-annotation-format.md plus user-docs/migration-guide.md clearly describes @supports, migration strategy, and usage patterns. All relevant Jest suites for valid-annotation-format, valid-req-reference, require-story-annotation, and require-req-annotation pass, confirming that the implemented behavior satisfies all acceptance criteria and detailed requirements from this story.
